name: Alfred Russel Wallace
summary: British naturalist, explorer, and co-discoverer of the principle of natural selection.

name: Henry Walter Bates
summary: English naturalist and explorer known for the theory of protective mimicry.

name: Charles Darwin
summary: English naturalist and primary proponent of the theory of evolution by natural selection.

name: Charles Lyell
summary: Scottish geologist and friend of Darwin who helped arrange the joint reading of evolutionary essays.

name: Joseph Hooker
summary: English botanist and friend of Darwin involved in the 1858 Linnean Society presentation.

name: Thomas Malthus
summary: English scholar whose ideas on human population controls influenced Wallace's theory of natural selection.

name: Philip L. Sclater
summary: English ornithologist who introduced the faunal regions scheme defended by Wallace.

name: Annie Mitten
summary: Spouse of Alfred Russel Wallace.

name: Roderick Murchison
summary: President of the Royal Geographical Society who praised Wallace's 1863 paper.

name: Percival Lowell
summary: Astronomer whose theory of Martian canals was debunked by Wallace.

name: Royal Geographical Society
summary: Learned society that granted Wallace funding and awarded him the Founder's Medal.

name: Linnean Society of London
summary: Scientific society where Wallace's and Darwin's essays on natural selection were jointly read.

name: Land Nationalisation Society
summary: Organization dedicated to land reform, of which Wallace was the first president.

name: Société de Géographie
summary: French geographical society that awarded Wallace the Gold Medal.

name: Helen
summary: Merchant vessel that caught fire and sank during Wallace's return from Brazil.

name: Jordeson
summary: Merchant vessel that carried Wallace back to England after the loss of the Helen.

name: Vestiges of the Natural History of Creation
summary: Anonymous work that converted Wallace and Bates to evolution.

name: A Narrative of Travels on the Amazon and Rio Negro
summary: Scientific travel narrative published by Wallace after his Amazon expedition.

name: Palm Trees of the Amazon and Their Uses
summary: Ethnobotanical work published by Wallace after his Amazon expedition.

name: On the Tendency of Varieties to Depart Indefinitely from the Original Type
summary: Essay by Wallace outlining the theory of natural selection.

name: On the Origin of Species
summary: Book by Darwin released in 1859 following the joint reading of evolutionary essays.

name: The Geographical Distribution of Animals
summary: Two-volume tome by Wallace reviewing principles of geographical distribution.

name: Tropical Nature and Other Essays
summary: Book of essays by Wallace focusing on the ecological biogeography of the tropics.

name: Island Life
summary: Book by Wallace discussing animal distribution and Ice Age causation.

name: Darwinism
summary: Book by Wallace discussing natural selection and corridor dispersal.

name: The Wonderful Century
summary: Book by Wallace outlining the nineteenth century's successes and failures.

name: Man's Place in the Universe
summary: Book by Wallace arguing Earth might be the only place with intelligent beings.

name: Is Mars Habitable?
summary: Book by Wallace debunking Lowell's theory of Martian canals.

name: The World of Life
summary: Book published by Wallace in 1910.

name: Usk, Monmouthshire
summary: Birthplace of Alfred Russel Wallace.

name: Broadstone, Dorset
summary: Place of death of Alfred Russel Wallace.

name: Amazon basin
summary: Region in South America where Wallace conducted early field work.

name: Malay Archipelago
summary: Region where Wallace conducted extensive field work and formulated natural selection.

name: Ternate
summary: Island in the Moluccas where Wallace wrote his essay on natural selection.

name: Sarawak
summary: Location where Wallace wrote his 1855 paper on species introduction.

name: Bedford Canal
summary: Location of Wallace's experiment proving the rotundity of the earth.
